summary: The PR aims to prevent HTTP header conflicts by avoiding setting `Content-Length` when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is present in `res.send()`. However, the implementation skips the entire chunk length calculation and Buffer conversion block when `Transfer-Encoding` is set, which causes automatic `ETag` generation to be incorrectly skipped as well.

findings.title: ETag header generation is skipped when Transfer-Encoding header is present
findings.description: In `lib/response.js`, `!this.get('Transfer-Encoding')` was added to the `if (chunk !== undefined)` condition. Because `len` calculation and string-to-Buffer conversion take place inside this conditional block, skipping this block when `Transfer-Encoding` is set leaves `len` as `undefined`. Consequently, the subsequent ETag population logic `if (generateETag && len !== undefined)` evaluates to `false`, causing Express to omit the `ETag` header whenever `Transfer-Encoding` is set. HTTP specifications (RFC 7232) state that `ETag` validators represent the resource representation and remain valid alongside transfer encodings like `chunked`.
findings.verificationHypothesis: Calling `res.set('Transfer-Encoding', 'chunked').send('hello')` with ETags enabled should produce a response containing an `ETag` header and omitting the `Content-Length` header. Currently, the `ETag` header is omitted.

suggestedReproduction.input: GET request to a route calling `res.set('Transfer-Encoding', 'chunked').send('hello world')` with app `etag` enabled.
suggestedReproduction.preconditions: Express app with default or enabled ETag setting.
suggestedReproduction.expectedBehavior: Response should contain an `ETag` header and must not contain a `Content-Length` header.
